chapters.name: Pawns
chapters.blurb: Humble foot soldiers. They only strike diagonally ahead.

chapters.name: Rooks
chapters.blurb: Straight lines, clean lanes. Learn how walls split the board.

chapters.name: Bishops
chapters.blurb: Diagonals only — and packings that use every last slant.

chapters.name: Knights
chapters.blurb: L-shaped jumps that leap over everything. Trust the colors.

chapters.name: Kings
chapters.blurb: No two kings on touching squares. Personal space, royally enforced.

chapters.name: Queens
chapters.blurb: The full classic ladder, up to the legendary Eight Queens.

chapters.name: Sudoku
chapters.blurb: Rows, columns and boxes join the battle. One piece each.

chapters.name: Mixed
chapters.blurb: Every piece type together. The true ChessDoku endgame.

levels.name: First Steps
levels.desc: Pawns attack only the two squares diagonally above them. Side by side is safe — diagonals are not.

levels.name: Marching Order
levels.desc: Six pawns. Remember: a whole column of pawns never quarrels.

levels.name: Phalanx
levels.desc: Eight pawns — the maximum a 4×4 board can hold. Form your ranks.

levels.name: Shield Wall
levels.desc: Twelve pawns around a cracked square. Keep the diagonals clear.

levels.name: The Great March
levels.desc: Fourteen pawns — a perfect march. Very few formations survive.

levels.name: Three Lanes
levels.desc: Rooks attack in straight lines. Give each rook its own row and its own column.

levels.name: Four Corners
levels.desc: One more rook, one more lane. Same idea, bigger board.

levels.name: The Pillar
levels.desc: A cracked square interrupts the lines — rooks cannot see through it.

levels.name: Crowded House
levels.desc: Six rooks but only five rows?! The cracked square splits a row — and a column — in two.

levels.name: Twin Pillars
levels.desc: Eight rooks on six rows. Use both cracked squares wisely.

levels.name: First Diagonals
levels.desc: Bishops only attack along diagonals. Rows and columns are perfectly safe.

levels.name: Slant Steps
levels.desc: Five bishops need five clear diagonal lanes.

levels.name: Full Fianchetto
levels.desc: Six bishops is the absolute maximum on a 4×4 board. Every diagonal counts.

levels.name: Diagonal Alley
levels.desc: Again the maximum: eight bishops on 5×5.

levels.name: Ten-Point Star
levels.desc: Ten bishops — a perfect pack. Think about the edges of the board.

levels.name: Little Hops
levels.desc: Knights jump in an L shape and leap over everything in between.

levels.name: Pony Club
levels.desc: Six knights, plenty of room — but their jumps cross the whole board.

levels.name: Full Stable
levels.desc: Eight knights — the maximum. Hint: a knight always lands on the opposite color.

levels.name: Cavalry Charge
levels.desc: Ten knights on 5×5. The color trick still works.

levels.name: The Great Herd
levels.desc: Twelve knights around a cracked square. Only a few arrangements exist.

levels.name: Polite Distance
levels.desc: Kings attack every touching square, diagonals included. Keep them apart.

levels.name: Royal Court
levels.desc: Seat all eight kings around the broken throne.

levels.name: Nine Thrones
levels.desc: Nine kings with room to spare — or so it seems.

levels.name: No Room to Breathe
levels.desc: Nine kings on a 5×5 board. Exactly ONE arrangement exists. Find it.

levels.name: Her Majesty
levels.desc: Queens attack rows, columns AND diagonals — the most dangerous piece of all.

levels.name: Queens Debut
levels.desc: The classic four-queens puzzle. Watch every diagonal.

levels.name: Five Crowns
levels.desc: Five queens, five rows — the pattern is a knight-like dance.

levels.name: Six Crowns
levels.desc: Only four arrangements exist on the whole 6×6 board.

levels.name: Seven Crowns
levels.desc: Seven queens. Trust the diagonal rhythm you have learned.

levels.name: The Eight Queens
levels.desc: The legendary puzzle from 1848, on a full chessboard.

levels.name: Sudoku School
levels.desc: New rule: every row and every column must hold exactly one piece. For rooks, that comes naturally.

levels.name: Knight Grid
levels.desc: Knights do not care about rows — but the sudoku rule does. One per row, one per column.

levels.name: Boxed Rooks
levels.desc: Box rule: exactly one rook inside each outlined 2×3 box.

levels.name: Center of Power
levels.desc: A queen is fixed in the center, like a sudoku given. One piece per row and column.

levels.name: Broken Board
levels.desc: Cracked squares block the queens' sight. One queen per outlined box.

levels.name: The Grand Grid
levels.desc: Eight queens, eight boxes, exactly one each. Only a fraction of the classic solutions obey the boxes.

levels.name: Odd Couple
levels.desc: Different pieces, different attacks. Rooks own the lines, bishops own the slants.

levels.name: Mixed Guard
levels.desc: Three piece types, one board. Each attacks in its own way.

levels.name: Around the Rook
levels.desc: A rook is nailed to the center. Build a peaceful court around it.

levels.name: Full House
levels.desc: Two of everything. A true test of coordination.

levels.name: The Whole Army
levels.desc: All six piece types on one board. Every rule you have learned applies at once.

levels.name: Grandmaster's Seal
levels.desc: The final challenge: four queens, two rooks, and their court on a full board. Good luck, Grandmaster.
